title: feat: select and manage installed agents from Models

commit.messageHeadline: feat(acp): integrate installed agents with shared model selection
refactor(acpx): delegate discovery and session permissions upstream
fix(acp): reconcile main and publish native assistant progress
perf(ui): defer native permission recovery until refusal
chore: reconcile ACP integration with current main
fix(acp): preserve model facts after empty native discovery
fix(acp): retain API catalogs across empty native refreshes
chore: reconcile generated config baseline with main
chore: reconcile main Telegram test fixtures
fix(acp): keep native preflight independent of agent execution
chore: reconcile current main configuration metadata
fix(acp): leave runtime availability with the execution owner
chore: reconcile main UI boot metadata for ACP landing
chore: resolve generated config conflicts for ACP landing

nodes.body:
Settings → Models now lists the supported installed agents and provides an enable switch for each one. Detection runs on the machine running OpenClaw. Each app owns its sign-in.

The browser checks cover detecting OpenCode, changing all four switches, persistence after reload with every switch off, and re-enabling OpenCode with the keyboard. Its model becomes available again. The registered native-process check also confirms that disabling an agent lets an admitted reply finish and refuses its next turn.

These captures use isolated local settings and a demo model. No paid inference or new Telegram run is included in this settings-control check.

Before:

![Models settings before installed-agent controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0d8b331-660d-4a0f-bf63-7a0b70e70f62)

After:

![Models settings with installed-agent controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd3f5450-ae24-4356-8ec4-8753bc33d3d8)

Source preview of the model-setup loading correction, before commit.

The loading view now reserves space for the installed-agent section. It shares the ready view's heading, text, and control sizes. Loading has no interactive controls and makes no model-catalog request. The existing 13px layout limit is unchanged; this source preview measured 8.14px.

Before, loading:

![Setup loading layout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/214a24df-a805-4c52-8b2f-69c4d92a5bc2)

Before, ready:

![Loaded setup layout before the correction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee018991-9da8-4cc8-bb29-fdf7e684dd04)

After, loading:

![Stable setup loading layout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dab91307-ac0e-4729-96a6-eb6f218f0980)

After, ready:

![Loaded setup layout after the correction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02bf80a5-d902-47ce-892a-15050d0a7c3b)

These captures use the real Control UI with a synthetic Gateway fixture. They do not run model inference.

Cold-session model authority passed all seven cases in the repair committed as [3a5fa39](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3a5fa39ae06237a9bad9c564105fb589cef84c5e).

The four active registrations selected the requested model once and prompted. Cancellation, timeout and revoked admission retained the initial model, sent no model control or prompt, produced no tool effect, and preserved the transcript from the held startup boundary.

The complete native phase below has 17 passing cases: seven cold-start cases, two queued-control cases, five tool-policy cases and three approval cases. It exercises the registered ACPX harness and published ACPX 0.17.0 through real child-process protocol peers. Vendor cloud behavior and paid inference are outside this proof.

Source: [cold cases and assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3a5fa39ae06237a9bad9c564105fb589cef84c5e/src/agents/harness/acp-native-execution.process.test.ts#L216), [approval cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3a5fa39ae06237a9bad9c564105fb589cef84c5e/src/agents/harness/acp-native-approval-effect.process.test.ts#L40).

The execution preceded the commit. Its final local-binding cleanup preserved all observations and assertions. At current head [d86adec](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d86adec8488897096721d618251c2c19008216dc), the native attempt and both protocol-peer fixtures remain byte-identical. Later test-only changes use the shared deferred helper and explicit fixture URLs; the cold-case inputs and assertions remain unchanged.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/harness/acp-native-execution.process.test.ts src/agents/harness/acp-native-approval-effect.process.test.ts extensions/acpx/src/runtime.test.ts extensions/acpx/src/runtime-owner.process.test.ts
```

### Cold-start cancellation through the Gateway

- Without cancellation, the same startup path applied Cedar Pro. OpenCode requested `opaque-beta` from the local model endpoint. The Gateway returned and stored the requested reply with Cedar Pro as the effective model.

Ready for maintainer merge at `f4a0d26b8f05e91f305d2a6cc887cfd94524c2ce`.

- Published ACPX **0.17.1** is integrated; the temporary Git dependency is gone.
- [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35502871726) is green. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`.
- Exact-head local ClawSweeper review passed: zero findings, security cleared, no maintainer/product decision remaining, tier B, sufficient proof.
- Retained evidence in the PR body covers published-driver upgrade, normal managed-plugin installation, native restart/reset and stale-consent rejection, real Telegram Test Server selection/persistence, real OpenCode compatibility, and inspected consent/automatic-retry/streaming screenshots.
- Final repairs keep native policy preflight independent of the full agent runner, preserve API catalogs through repeated empty native discovery, and leave runtime availability and explicit pins with their existing execution owner. Temporary fixture workarounds were removed.

The disclosed custom bundled-Darwin packaging and unexercised rollback/MCP limits remain as documented. No OpenClaw merge, package release, or operator Gateway redeployment was performed.

Landed as 8cd38b03ceb822718ab2e5e1693340f15df22b14 through a normal squash merge, without admin bypass.

Installed-agent selection now uses published ACPX 0.17.1. Enabling an agent no longer waits for discovery; explicit per-chat consent retries the refused message automatically, while mandatory boundaries and explicit billing routes remain intact.
